name: pal-mcp-server

tools.name: chat
tools.description: Use as a collaborative thinking partner: brainstorm, second opinions, idea validation with another model. Not for tasks that need no outside perspective.

prompt.description: Question or idea for the external model, with context: goal, what you tried, blockers. No large inline code; pass file paths in absolute_file_paths.

absolute_file_paths.description: Absolute paths of code files to share.

images.description: Absolute image paths or base64, for visual context.

working_directory_absolute_path.description: Existing directory (absolute path) for generated code artifacts.

model.description: Auto model selection. If the user names a model, pass that exact name unless the server rejects it; otherwise choose one (`listmodels` reviews options).

continuation_id.description: Thread ID for multi-turn conversations; works across tools. Always reuse the last one you were given so context, files, and findings carry over.

tools.name: clink
tools.description: Run a request through an external AI CLI (e.g. claude, codex, gemini; see cli_name) and return its answer. Use when the user asks for that CLI or wants an independent review or plan from it.

prompt.description: Request for the CLI; conversation context is pre-applied.

role.description: Role preset (default 'default'). Roles: codereviewer, default, planner (all CLIs).

images.description: Absolute image paths or base64 blobs.

continuation_id.description: Thread ID for multi-turn conversations; works across tools. Always reuse the last one you were given so context, files, and findings carry over.

tools.name: jules
tools.description: Drive Google Jules, an async coding agent on a connected GitHub repo. One non-blocking action per call: list_sources, create, status, message, approve. Needs JULES_API_KEY. Not for edits to the local checkout.

action.description: list_sources: discover repos; create: start a session; status: poll state, activities, PR; message: steer a running session; approve: approve the pending plan; archive: hide a session from the default list view; unarchive: restore it.

starting_branch.description: Base branch (create); defaults to the repo default branch.

session_id.description: Session id for status/message/approve/archive/unarchive; raw or 'sessions/{id}'.

require_plan_approval.description: Create: wait for action=approve before executing.

automation_mode.description: Create: AUTO_CREATE_PR opens a pull request automatically.

tools.name: thinkdeep
tools.description: Multi-step investigation and reasoning with expert-model validation. Use for architecture decisions, hard bugs, performance or security analysis. Not for questions you can answer directly.

step.description: Content and findings of the current step.

next_step_required.description: True if another step follows; when false, set total_steps equal to step_number.

findings.description: Findings and evidence from this step.

relevant_files.description: Relevant files or folders as full absolute paths; do not shorten.

issues_found.description: Issues found, each with a severity level.

confidence.description: Confidence in your analysis: exploring, low, medium, high, very_high, almost_certain or certain. certain skips expert validation; use very_high or almost_certain when not fully verified.

hypothesis.description: Current theory about the issue or goal.

use_assistant_model.description: Call the assistant model for expert analysis after the workflow steps. False skips it and relies only on your own investigation.

continuation_id.description: Thread ID for multi-turn conversations; works across tools. Always reuse the last one you were given so context, files, and findings carry over.

images.description: Absolute image paths or base64 blobs.

model.description: Auto model selection. If the user names a model, pass that exact name unless the server rejects it; otherwise choose one (`listmodels` reviews options).

problem_context.description: Extra context on the problem or goal.

focus_areas.description: Focus areas, e.g. architecture, performance, security.

tools.name: planner
tools.description: Sequential planning with revision and branching; makes no model call. Use for multi-step project, migration or architecture plans. Not for tasks you can act on directly.

step.description: Step 1: the task, problem and scope. Later steps: updates, revisions, branches, or open questions that shape the plan.

next_step_required.description: True if another step follows; when false, set total_steps equal to step_number.

continuation_id.description: Thread ID for multi-turn conversations; works across tools. Always reuse the last one you were given so context, files, and findings carry over.

model.description: Auto model selection. If the user names a model, pass that exact name unless the server rejects it; otherwise choose one (`listmodels` reviews options).

is_step_revision.description: True when replacing an earlier step.

is_branch_point.description: True when this step starts an alternative branch.

branch_from_step.description: Step number the branch starts from.

more_steps_needed.description: True when more steps than estimated are needed.

tools.name: consensus
tools.description: Sends one proposal to several models with for/against/neutral stances; returns each answer for you to synthesize. Use for design or technology decisions needing independent views. Not for decisions with one clear answer.

step.description: Step 1: the exact proposal every model sees, phrased as 'Evaluate…' (no meta commentary). Steps 2+: notes on the latest response; never sent to other models.

step_number.description: Starts at 1. Step 1: your own analysis; steps 2+: one model response each.

total_steps.description: Models consulted plus one final synthesis step.

next_step_required.description: True while consultations remain; false when ready to synthesize.

findings.description: Step 1: your own analysis, kept for synthesis (not shared with models). Steps 2+: summary of the newest response.

relevant_files.description: Optional supporting files; absolute, non-abbreviated paths.

continuation_id.description: Thread ID for multi-turn conversations; works across tools. Always reuse the last one you were given so context, files, and findings carry over.

images.description: Optional absolute image paths or base64 references.

models.description: Models to consult, at least two. Entry keys: model, stance (for/against/neutral), stance_prompt. (model, stance) pairs must be unique, e.g. [{'model':'gpt5','stance':'for'}, {'model':'pro','stance':'against'}]. If the user names a model, use that exact value or report the provider error; never substitute. `listmodels` lists the roster. No models detected; configure provider credentials or check `listmodels`.

current_model_index.description: 0-based index of the next model to consult (managed internally).

model_responses.description: Internal log of responses gathered so far.

tools.name: codereview
tools.description: Multi-step code review with expert-model validation: quality, security, performance, architecture. Use to review a change set or module. Not for fixes you can make directly.

step.description: Step 1: review strategy. Later: findings across quality, security, performance and architecture. Reference code via relevant_files; no large snippets.

total_steps.description: 2 steps for external validation (analysis, summary), 1 for internal; same limits when continuing via continuation_id.

next_step_required.description: external: True on step 1, False on step 2; internal: False immediately. Same on continuations.

findings.description: Findings so far, positive and negative; revise each step.

files_checked.description: Absolute paths of all files examined, ruled-out ones included.

relevant_files.description: Step 1: all files or directories under review, required; full absolute paths, do not shorten. Final step: only files tied to key findings.

hypothesis.description: Current theory about the issue or goal.

use_assistant_model.description: Call the assistant model for expert analysis after the workflow steps. False skips it and relies only on your own investigation.

continuation_id.description: Thread ID for multi-turn conversations; works across tools. Always reuse the last one you were given so context, files, and findings carry over.

images.description: Optional absolute paths to diagrams or screenshots.

model.description: Auto model selection. If the user names a model, pass that exact name unless the server rejects it; otherwise choose one (`listmodels` reviews options).

review_validation_type.description: external (default) adds an expert-model follow-up; internal is local only.

standards.description: Standards or style guide to enforce.

tools.name: precommit
tools.description: Validates git changes before a commit or merge (diff, impact, security, completeness) with expert validation. Use before commits, also across repos; compare_to diffs vs a ref. Not for code outside a diff; use codereview.

step.description: Step 1: how you will validate the changes. Later: findings on diffs and impact. Reference code via relevant_files; no large snippets.

total_steps.description: Up to 3 steps for external validation (analysis, follow-ups, summary), 1 for internal; same limits when resuming via continuation_id.

next_step_required.description: False when validation is complete. If total_steps >= 3 or precommit_type is external, stay True until the final step; same on continuations.

findings.description: Diff insights, risks, missing tests, security concerns and positives; revise each step.

files_checked.description: Absolute paths of all files examined, ruled-out ones included.

relevant_files.description: Files in the change or its validation (code, config, tests, docs); full absolute paths, do not shorten.

hypothesis.description: Current theory about the issue or goal.

use_assistant_model.description: Call the assistant model for expert analysis after the workflow steps. False skips it and relies only on your own investigation.

continuation_id.description: Thread ID for multi-turn conversations; works across tools. Always reuse the last one you were given so context, files, and findings carry over.

images.description: Optional absolute paths to screenshots or diagrams.

model.description: Auto model selection. If the user names a model, pass that exact name unless the server rejects it; otherwise choose one (`listmodels` reviews options).

precommit_type.description: external (default) adds an expert-model follow-up; internal is local only.

path.description: Absolute path to the repo root. Required in step 1.

compare_to.description: Git ref to diff against; default is staged/unstaged changes.

include_staged.description: Inspect staged changes; ignored when compare_to is set.

include_unstaged.description: Inspect unstaged changes; ignored when compare_to is set.

focus_on.description: Emphasis, e.g. security, performance, test coverage.

tools.name: debug
tools.description: Multi-step debugging and root cause analysis with expert-model validation. Use for bugs with an unclear cause: errors, performance, races, leaks, integration failures. Not for issues you can fix directly.

step.description: Step 1: the issue and direction. Later: trace dependencies, test hypotheses. Symptoms can mislead; 'no bug' is valid. Text only; code goes in relevant_files.

total_steps.description: Estimated steps to finish; adjust as findings emerge. When continuation_id is set, use 1.

next_step_required.description: False when the root cause is known or the investigation is complete; this triggers expert analysis. When continuation_id is set, use False.

findings.description: Clues, code/log evidence, disproven theories; be specific. 'No bug found' is a valid result.

files_checked.description: Absolute paths of all files examined, ruled-out ones included.

relevant_files.description: Absolute paths of files where the issue is caused, triggered or manifests.

issues_found.description: Issues found, each with a severity level.

confidence.description: Confidence in the hypothesis. Use certain only when root cause and fix are both confirmed locally: it skips external model validation. If nearly but not fully sure, use very_high or almost_certain.

hypothesis.description: Root cause theory from evidence; revisable. 'No bug found' or 'symptoms unrelated to code' are valid if supported.

use_assistant_model.description: Call the assistant model for expert analysis after the workflow steps. False skips it and relies only on your own investigation.

continuation_id.description: Thread ID for multi-turn conversations; works across tools. Always reuse the last one you were given so context, files, and findings carry over.

images.description: Optional absolute paths to screenshots or visuals.

model.description: Auto model selection. If the user names a model, pass that exact name unless the server rejects it; otherwise choose one (`listmodels` reviews options).

tools.name: secaudit
tools.description: Step-by-step security audit with expert validation. Use for OWASP Top 10 review, compliance checks, threat modeling, or security architecture review. Not for a single known vulnerability you can fix directly.

step.description: Step 1: outline the audit strategy (OWASP Top 10, auth, validation). Later steps: report findings. Reference code via relevant_files; do not paste large snippets.

total_steps.description: Estimated audit steps; adjust as risks surface.

next_step_required.description: True while analysis continues; False when ready to hand off for expert validation.

findings.description: Vulnerabilities, auth issues, validation gaps, compliance notes, and positives; revise earlier findings as needed.

files_checked.description: All files examined (absolute paths), including ones ruled out.

relevant_files.description: Security-relevant files (absolute paths): auth, configs, sensitive code.

issues_found.description: Security issues as objects with 'severity' (critical/high/medium/low) and 'description'.

confidence.description: 'certain' skips external validation; use it only when the audit is fully complete.

hypothesis.description: Current theory about the issue or goal.

use_assistant_model.description: Call the assistant model for expert analysis after the workflow steps. False skips it and relies only on your own investigation.

continuation_id.description: Thread ID for multi-turn conversations; works across tools. Always reuse the last one you were given so context, files, and findings carry over.

images.description: Optional absolute paths to diagrams or threat models.

model.description: Auto model selection. If the user names a model, pass that exact name unless the server rejects it; otherwise choose one (`listmodels` reviews options).

security_scope.description: Security context: app type (web, mobile, API, cloud), stack, user types, data sensitivity, threat landscape.

threat_level.description: Assessed threat level: low (internal), medium (customer-facing/business data), high (regulated or sensitive), critical (financial/healthcare/PII).

compliance_requirements.description: Applicable compliance frameworks, e.g. SOC2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, ISO 27001, NIST.

tools.name: docgen
tools.description: Guides file-by-file documentation of a codebase: docstrings, Big O complexity, call flow, inline comments. Use to document one file or many. Not for a single docstring you can write directly.

step.description: Content and findings of the current step.

next_step_required.description: True if another step follows; when false, set total_steps equal to step_number.

findings.description: Findings and evidence from this step.

relevant_files.description: Relevant files or folders as full absolute paths; do not shorten.

issues_found.description: Issues found, each with a severity level.

continuation_id.description: Thread ID for multi-turn conversations; works across tools. Always reuse the last one you were given so context, files, and findings carry over.

document_flow.description: Include call flow and dependency notes.

update_existing.description: Update inaccurate or outdated docs rather than leaving them.

comments_on_complex_logic.description: Add inline comments around non-obvious logic.

num_files_documented.description: Files fully documented so far; increment only when a file is complete.

total_files_to_document.description: Files identified in discovery; completion requires matching this count.

tools.name: analyze
tools.description: Step-by-step code analysis with expert validation. Use for architecture, performance, maintainability or pattern assessment of a codebase. Not for a lookup answerable from a single file.

step.description: Step 1: state the strategy (how you will map structure, business logic, quality, performance, architecture). Later steps: report findings and adapt the plan.

step_number.description: Current step index, starting at 1. Each step builds on or revises the previous one.

total_steps.description: Estimated steps to complete the analysis; adjust as findings emerge.

next_step_required.description: True to continue with another step. False means the analysis is complete and ready for expert validation.

findings.description: Discoveries this step: architecture, tech stack, scalability, performance, maintainability, improvement opportunities. Record both strengths and concerns (tech debt, overengineering, needless complexity). Later steps confirm or revise earlier findings.

files_checked.description: All files examined (absolute paths), including ones ruled out.

relevant_files.description: Subset of files_checked bearing on the findings (absolute paths): key patterns, architectural decisions, improvement opportunities. Required in step 1.

issues_found.description: Issues found, as objects with 'severity' (critical, high, medium, low) and 'description'.

use_assistant_model.description: Call the assistant model for expert analysis after the workflow steps. False skips it and relies only on your own investigation.

continuation_id.description: Thread ID for multi-turn conversations; works across tools. Always reuse the last one you were given so context, files, and findings carry over.

images.description: Optional absolute paths to architecture diagrams or other visual references.

model.description: Auto model selection. If the user names a model, pass that exact name unless the server rejects it; otherwise choose one (`listmodels` reviews options).

confidence.description: Confidence in the analysis. 'certain' means the analysis is complete and ready for validation.

tools.name: refactor
tools.description: Step-by-step refactoring analysis with expert validation. Use for code smell detection, decomposition planning, modernization, or maintainability improvements. Not for edits you can make yourself.

step.description: Step 1: state the strategy. Later steps: report findings on smells and decomposition, modernization, and organization opportunities. Reference code via relevant_files; do not paste large snippets.

step_number.description: Current step index, starting at 1. Each step builds on or revises the previous one.

total_steps.description: Estimated steps to complete the investigation; adjust as opportunities emerge.

next_step_required.description: True to continue with another step. False means the refactoring analysis is complete and ready for expert validation.

findings.description: Discoveries this step: code smells and decomposition, modernization, or organization opportunities. Note strengths and weaknesses. Later steps confirm or revise earlier findings.

files_checked.description: All files examined (absolute paths), including ones ruled out.

relevant_files.description: Subset of files_checked needing refactoring (absolute paths). Required in step 1.

issues_found.description: Refactoring opportunities as objects with 'severity' (critical/high/medium/low), 'type' (codesmells/decompose/modernize/organization), and 'description'.

confidence.description: exploring (starting), incomplete (much work remains), partial (some opportunities found, more analysis needed), complete (all major opportunities identified). 'complete' skips expert validation; use it only when you can recommend without expert help. Prefer 'partial' for large files or uncertain analysis.

hypothesis.description: Current theory about the issue or goal.

use_assistant_model.description: Call the assistant model for expert analysis after the workflow steps. False skips it and relies only on your own investigation.

continuation_id.description: Thread ID for multi-turn conversations; works across tools. Always reuse the last one you were given so context, files, and findings carry over.

images.description: Optional absolute paths to diagrams, mockups, or design documents. Include only if they materially help.

model.description: Auto model selection. If the user names a model, pass that exact name unless the server rejects it; otherwise choose one (`listmodels` reviews options).

refactor_type.description: Kind of refactoring analysis to perform.

style_guide_examples.description: Optional files or folders showing the target coding style. Full absolute paths; do not shorten.

tools.name: tracer
tools.description: Guided, systematic code tracing: precision mode (execution flow, call chains) or dependencies mode (structural relationships). Use to map how a method, class or module connects to the codebase. Not for a one-grep lookup.

step.description: Content and findings of the current step.

next_step_required.description: True if another step follows; when false, set total_steps equal to step_number.

findings.description: Findings and evidence from this step.

relevant_files.description: Relevant files or folders as full absolute paths; do not shorten.

confidence.description: Confidence in your findings so far: exploring, low, medium, high, very_high, almost_certain or certain.

continuation_id.description: Thread ID for multi-turn conversations; works across tools. Always reuse the last one you were given so context, files, and findings carry over.

images.description: Optional paths to architecture diagrams or flow charts.

model.description: Auto model selection. If the user names a model, pass that exact name unless the server rejects it; otherwise choose one (`listmodels` reviews options).

trace_mode.description: 'precision' (execution flow), 'dependencies' (structural relationships), or 'ask' to have the user choose in step 1.

target_description.description: What to trace and why; include what you are trying to understand.

tools.name: testgen
tools.description: Generates framework-specific tests with edge-case coverage for named functions, classes, or modules. Scope to specific components, not the whole codebase. Not for running tests or debugging a failing one.

step.description: Step 1: outline how you will analyse structure, business logic, critical paths, and edge cases. Later steps: record findings and new scenarios.

step_number.description: Current step, starting at 1; each builds on prior work.

total_steps.description: Estimated steps for test planning; adjust as scenarios appear.

next_step_required.description: True while planning continues; False when the test plan is ready for expert validation.

findings.description: Functionality, critical paths, edge cases, boundary conditions, error handling, and existing test patterns; cover happy and failure paths.

files_checked.description: All files examined (absolute paths), including ones ruled out.

relevant_files.description: Absolute paths of code needing new or updated tests (plus dependencies, existing fixtures). Required in step 1.

issues_found.description: Issues found, each with a severity level.

confidence.description: Confidence in the test plan. 'certain' means the plan is complete with every scenario identified, and skips external model validation; if not fully sure, use 'very_high' or 'almost_certain' instead.

hypothesis.description: Current theory about the issue or goal.

use_assistant_model.description: Call the assistant model for expert analysis after the workflow steps. False skips it and relies only on your own investigation.

continuation_id.description: Thread ID for multi-turn conversations; works across tools. Always reuse the last one you were given so context, files, and findings carry over.

images.description: Optional absolute paths to diagrams of the system under test.

model.description: Auto model selection. If the user names a model, pass that exact name unless the server rejects it; otherwise choose one (`listmodels` reviews options).

tools.name: challenge
tools.description: Replaces reflexive agreement with critical thinking and reasoned analysis. Trigger automatically when the user critically questions, disagrees with or pushes back on an earlier answer; manually on contentious claims.

prompt.description: Statement to scrutinize. Manual: drop the word 'challenge', pass the statement only. Automatic: pass the full user message unmodified.

tools.name: apilookup
tools.description: Current API/SDK docs, versions, breaking changes, deprecations, migration guides and release notes from authoritative sources. Use automatically when currency matters; not for stable basics.

prompt.description: API, SDK, library, framework or other technology to look up and what you need (docs, version, breaking changes, migration).

instructions: When the user names a specific model (e.g. 'use chat with gpt5'), send that exact model in the tool call. When no model is mentioned, first use the `listmodels` tool from PAL to obtain available models to choose the best one from.
